text: Provides the same tools, agent loop, and context management as Claude Code, programmable via Python and TypeScript SDKs
quote: The Agent SDK gives you the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code, programmable in Python and TypeScript.

text: Ships built-in tools to read, write, edit files, run shell commands, and search the web
quote: Built-in tools | Read, write, edit files, run commands, and search the web

text: Hooks let you run custom callback code in response to agent events like tool calls or session start/stop
quote: Hooks are callback functions that run your code in response to agent events, like a tool being called, a session starting, or execution stopping.

text: Hooks can block dangerous operations, like destructive shell commands, before they execute
quote: With hooks, you can: Block dangerous operations before they execute, like destructive shell commands or unauthorized file access

text: Subagents are separate agent instances the main agent can spawn to isolate context and run parallel focused analyses
quote: Subagents are separate agent instances that your main agent can spawn to handle focused subtasks. Use them to isolate context, run multiple analyses in parallel, and apply specialized instructions

text: Via MCP, agents can query databases and integrate with APIs like Slack and GitHub without custom tool code
quote: With MCP, your agent can query databases, integrate with APIs like Slack and GitHub, and connect to other services without writing custom tool implementations.

text: Permission modes and rules let you define what tool usage is auto-allowed vs requires runtime handling
quote: The Claude Agent SDK provides permission controls to manage how Claude uses tools. Use permission modes and rules to define what's allowed automatically, and the canUseTool callback to handle everything else at runtime.

text: Sessions accumulate conversation history and are automatically persisted to disk for later resumption
quote: A session is the conversation history the SDK accumulates while your agent works. ... The SDK writes it to disk automatically so you can return to it later.

text: Custom tools let developers define their own functions that Claude can call during a conversation
quote: Custom tools extend the Agent SDK by letting you define your own functions that Claude can call during a conversation.

text: A canUseTool callback fires whenever Claude needs permission/user input before using a tool
quote: Pass a canUseTool callback in your query options. The callback fires whenever Claude needs user input, receiving the tool name and input as arguments

text: Structured outputs let you define a schema and get back validated JSON matching it
quote: Structured outputs let you define the exact shape of data you want back from an agent. ... you still get validated JSON matching your schema at the end.

text: Docs cover production deployment: subprocess architecture, session persistence, scaling, observability, multi-tenant isolation for Docker/K8s/sandboxes
quote: Deploy the Agent SDK in production: subprocess architecture, session persistence, scaling, observability, and multi-tenant isolation for Docker, Kubernetes, and sandbox providers.

text: Streaming input mode is the preferred interaction pattern, enabling rich interactive agent experiences
quote: Streaming input mode is the preferred way to use the Claude Agent SDK. It provides full access to the agent's capabilities and enables rich, interactive experiences.

text: ClaudeSDKClient is provided for interactive applications such as chat interfaces where next action depends on Claude's response
quote: Use ClaudeSDKClient for interactive applications such as chat interfaces, or when the next action depends on Claude's response.

text: The Claude Code CLI is bundled automatically with the SDK package, requiring no separate installation
quote: The Claude Code CLI is automatically bundled with the package - no separate installation required! The SDK will use the bundled CLI by default.

text: Claude can ask clarifying questions to the user via a built-in AskUserQuestion tool
quote: Claude requests user input in two situations: when it needs permission to use a tool (like deleting files or running commands), and when it has clarifying questions (via the AskUserQuestion tool).

text: Streaming sessions support attaching images directly to messages for visual analysis
quote: In streaming input mode, you work in a persistent session with these capabilities: Image uploads: attach images directly to messages for visual analysis and understanding

text: SDK spawns and supervises a claude CLI subprocess that owns a shell, working directory, and on-disk session files
quote: The Agent SDK spawns and supervises a claude CLI subprocess that owns a shell, a working directory, and session files on disk.

text: Sessions can be forked, creating a new session with a copy of the original's history while the original remains intact
quote: Fork is different: it creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history. The original stays

text: SDK supports long-lived agent processes that handle interruptions, surface permission requests, and manage sessions
quote: It allows the agent to operate as a long lived process that takes in user input, handles interruptions, surfaces permission requests, and handles session management.

text: A SessionStore adapter can mirror session transcripts to your own backend so sessions can resume on a different host
quote: A `SessionStore` adapter lets you mirror those transcripts to your own backend, such as an object store, a key-value store, or a database, so a session created on one host can be resumed on another host running from a matching working direc

text: SDK supports interrupting an in-progress agent run
quote: Interrupts | ❌ Not supported | ✅ Supported

text: Same filesystem-based project features as Claude Code are available: CLAUDE.md project instructions, rules, skills, and hooks
quote: The Agent SDK is built on the same foundation as Claude Code, which means your SDK agents have access to the same filesystem-based features: project instructions (`CLAUDE.md` and rules), skills, hooks, and more.

text: Claude Code offers five concurrency patterns for multi-task work: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows, and projects
quote: Claude Code has five ways to work on several tasks at once: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows, and projects.

text: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, tool access, and independent permissions
quote: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.

text: Agent view (`claude agents`) gives one screen showing all background sessions' status and pending input needs
quote: Agent view, opened with `claude agents`, is one screen for all your background sessions: what's running, what needs your input, and what's done.

text: Agent teams let multiple Claude Code instances coordinate work with one session acting as team lead assigning tasks
quote: Agent teams let you coordinate multiple Claude Code instances working together. One session acts as the team lead, coordinating work, assigning tasks, and synthesizing results.

text: Administrators can restrict which MCP servers are allowed org-wide or disable MCP entirely
quote: As an administrator, you can restrict which servers run in your organization, from deploying a fixed approved set to disabling MCP entirely, and you can provide servers to every user.

text: An in-process MCP server lets the SDK app give Claude access to databases, external APIs, or custom domain logic
quote: Using the SDK's in-process MCP server, you can give Claude access to databases, external APIs, domain-specific logic, or any other capability your application needs.

text: MCP servers can run as local processes, over HTTP, or in-process within the SDK application
quote: MCP servers can run as local processes, connect over HTTP, or execute directly within your SDK application.

text: Subagents can be defined programmatically via the `agents` parameter in query() options
quote: You can create subagents in three ways: Programmatically: use the `agents` parameter in your `query()` options.

text: Official example applications are provided: a TypeScript demos repo and Python recipes in the Claude Cookbook
quote: TypeScript applications live in the `claude-agent-sdk-demos` repo, and Python recipes live in the Claude Cookbook.

text: Skills are defined via a SKILL.md file that Claude adds to its toolkit and can invoke directly with /skill-name
quote: Create a `SKILL.md` file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit. Claude uses skills when relevant, or you can invoke one directly with `/skill-name`.

text: SDK exposes a simple async query() streaming API that yields message objects like AssistantMessage as the agent runs
quote:
async for message in query(prompt="Hello Claude"):
    if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage):

text: Streaming can be enabled by setting includePartialMessages/include_partial_messages to true in query options
quote: To enable streaming, set `include_partial_messages` (Python) or `includePartialMessages` (TypeScript) to `true` in your options.

text: Both permission and clarifying-question prompts route through the same canUseTool callback that pauses execution until a response is returned
quote: Both trigger your `canUseTool` callback, which pauses execution until you return a response.

text: Resuming a session gives the agent full prior context: files already read, analysis already performed, decisions already made
quote: Returning to a session means the agent has full context from before: files it already read, analysis it already performed, decisions it already made.
